newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees supply deficits in oils and meals.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees supply deficits in oils and meals.

text.p: World output of 17 oils and fats in 1996/97 was pegged at 97.5 million tonnes compared with 96.1 million in 95/96, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
The market would move into a deficit, with consumption in 96/97 seen at 98.5 million tonnes versus 95.3 million in 95/96.
Oil World revised upwards its September output estimate of 97.3 million for 96/97 and the 95/96 estimate in September of 95.6 million.
It cited larger oilseeds crops, but added their possible effect on oils output was lessened by lower implied oil yields.
Demand impulses were seen stemming from population and income growth and lower use of oils in non-food applications.
The 96/97 season would also bring an output deficit in 12 key oilmeals, where higher consumption at 169.1 million tonnes compared with 166.9 previously, Oil World said.
Soymeal's share in the usage total was put at 53.5 percent.
Consumption would be led by Chinese and other Asian soymeal demand while in the EU-15, soymeal demand was forecast to fall because of high prices versus feed grain.
Global production of meals in 96/97 was estimated at 167.9 million compared with 166.9 million in 95/96.
